WITH patient_lab AS (
  SELECT l.ID, l.Date, p.SEX, l.ALB, l.UN, l.`T-BIL`
  FROM Laboratory l
  INNER JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID
),
patient_level AS (
  SELECT 
    ID,
    SEX,
    AVG(ALB) as avg_alb,
    AVG(CASE WHEN UN IS NOT NULL AND `T-BIL` IS NOT NULL AND `T-BIL` != 0 THEN (UN * 1.0) / `T-BIL` ELSE NULL END) as avg_un_tbil_ratio
  FROM patient_lab
  GROUP BY ID, SEX
),
sex_level AS (
  SELECT 
    SEX,
    AVG(avg_alb) as sex_avg_alb,
    AVG(avg_un_tbil_ratio) as sex_avg_un_tbil_ratio
  FROM patient_level
  GROUP BY SEX
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(sex_avg_alb) as overall_mean_alb
  FROM sex_level
)
SELECT 
  sl.SEX,
  sl.sex_avg_alb as average_ALB,
  sl.sex_avg_un_tbil_ratio as average_UN_per_TBIL_ratio,
  sl.sex_avg_alb - om.overall_mean_alb as above_mean
FROM sex_level sl, overall_mean om
WHERE sl.sex_avg_alb > om.overall_mean_alb
ORDER BY sl.SEX    -- The results from round 2 show both 'F' and 'M' have ALB above the overall mean (4.053), with M being further above mean than F
